as_written_in_papers.quote: Direct sequencing of LCAT gene and comparison with reference sequence (NM_000229) revealed that Case 1 had a C to T nucleotide substitution in Exon 2 resulting in Pro69Leu [c.278 C>T (p.Pro69Leu)] (Figure 1C) and Case 2 had a T to C substitution in Exon 6 resulting in Met293Thr mutations [c.950 T>C (p.Met293Thr)] (Figure 1D).
Nucleotide sequence analysis of the LCAT gene revealed that he is homozygous to a missense mutation (c. 278C > T [p. P69L]) in exon 2 of the LCAT gene [29].

cases.statement: One person, reported twice: Case 1 of 25984174 (27-year-old Japanese man, consanguineous parents) and the gene-therapy patient of 36387451 (34-year-old Japanese man), who cites 25984174 for his genotype; the pipeline merged them as LCAT-ID0080.

people.label: Case 1
people.key_phenotypes: Bilateral corneal opacity; mild normochromic anemia (11.3 g/dL); proteinuria 0.21 g/day with normal renal function; HDL-C 3 mg/dL and very low LDL-C; renal biopsy with lipid deposits in the GBM.

quotes.quote: A 27-year-old Japanese man was referred to Okayama University Hospital because he had extremely low HDL-C and LDL-C concentrations.
On physical examination, he showed bilateral corneal opacity, but no other abnormal findings.
Laboratory findings demonstrated a mild degree of normochoromic-normocytotic anemia (11.3 g/dL).
Although his renal function was normal, (+1) proteinuria was revealed via the dipstick method (0.21 g/day).
The consanguinity was found in his parents as shown in Figure 1A.

people.key_phenotypes: FLD with markedly low HDL-C and LDL-C, bilateral corneal opacity, proteinuria that later increased, mild anemia, GBM lipid deposits.

quotes.quote: A 34-year-old Japanese man previously diagnosed with FLD based on LCAT gene analysis, markedly low HDL-C and LDL-cholesterol (LDL-C), bilateral corneal opacity, and modest proteinuria willingly participated in this study.
Nucleotide sequence analysis of the LCAT gene revealed that he is homozygous to a missense mutation (c. 278C > T [p. P69L]) in exon 2 of the LCAT gene [29].
Electron microscopic analysis of the renal biopsy specimen revealed lipid deposits with a vacuolar lucent appearance in the glomerular basement membrane [29].
The patient had mild anemia when he was diagnosed at the age of 30 (blood hemoglobin level = 11.3 g/dL; grade I).
Before participating in the clinical study, the patient rapidly developed proteinuria, the main reason for deciding to receive LCAT-GMAC implantation.

Katayama A., Wada J., Kataoka H.U., et al, 2011, Two novel mutations of lecithin:cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT) gene and the influence of APOE genotypes on clinical manifestations, NDT Plus PMID:25984174

phenotype_specificity.statement: Corneal opacity, anemia, proteinuria with GBM lipid deposits and very low HDL-C, described as FLD; plasma LCAT activity about half normal, which the authors note suggests FED. No testing of other genes is reported.

quotes.quote: On physical examination, he showed bilateral corneal opacity, but no other abnormal findings.
Laboratory findings demonstrated a mild degree of normochoromic-normocytotic anemia (11.3 g/dL).

Renal biopsy in both cases revealed similar histological findings; diffuse vacuolization of the glomerular basement membranes (GBM) by periodic acid-methenamine silver stain and lipid deposits with a vacuolar lucent appearance in the mesangial matrix and the GBM by electron microscopy (Figure 1E and F).

In both cases, half normal LCAT activity was observed by using exogenous substrate, suggesting the diagnosis of FED. However, clinical manifestations with hemolytic anemia and renal involvement coincided with the features of FLD.
In conclusion, we describe two unrelated FLD patients with corneal opacity, hemolytic anemia, abnormalities in serum lipoprotein profile and lipid accumulation in GBM.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Predicted consequence from the batch HGVS: missense, p.(Pro93Leu); the papers state p.Pro69Leu / p.P69L in exon 2, and 36387451 calls it a missense mutation. Both papers describe FLD as autosomal recessive, caused by loss of LCAT activity.

quotes.quote: Here, we describe two novel mutations of LCAT gene, a C to T transition in Exon 2 converting proline 69 to leucine (Pro69Leu) and a T to C transition in Exon 6 converting methionine 293 to threonine (Met293Thr).
Nucleotide sequence analysis of the LCAT gene revealed that he is homozygous to a missense mutation (c. 278C > T [p. P69L]) in exon 2 of the LCAT gene [29].

Familial lecithin:cholesterol acyltransferase deficiency (FLD) is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by corneal opacity, hemolytic anemia, low high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) and proteinuria.
The loss of LCAT activity leads to increased levels of phosphatidylcholine and free cholesterol (FC) in the blood and to the formation of an abnormal lipoprotein called lipoprotein-X (Lp-X).
The LCAT gene disorder is an autosomal recessive trait, and its prevalence is less than one in a million.

authors_classification.statement: 25984174 calls it a novel LCAT mutation; no ACMG classification in either paper.

quotes.quote: Two novel lecithin:cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT) mutations
Two novel lecithin:cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT) mutations[c.278 C>T (p.Pro69Leu); c.950 T>C (p.Met293Thr)] were identified in a 27-year-old man and in a 30-year-old woman, respectively.

concerns: Protein numbering differs: both papers state p.Pro69Leu (P69L), the batch predicts p.(Pro93Leu) from c.278C>T on NM_000229.2. The 24-residue difference is consistent with mature-protein (legacy) numbering, but neither paper says so; cDNA and exon agree with the batch.

Same person in two papers: 36387451 cites 25984174 [29] for the genotype and renal biopsy. Ages differ: 25984174 describes a 27-year-old at referral, while 36387451 says he was diagnosed at age 30 (both give hemoglobin 11.3 g/dL). The merge looks right, but the age at diagnosis conflicts.
The text says both parents were heterozygous, but it also says the father's DNA was not available; only the mother was tested.
Transcript stated only as NM_000229 (no version).
notes_for_panel: One homozygous Japanese FLD patient from a consanguineous family, reported twice; only the mother was genotyped. The 36387451 gene-therapy follow-up adds clinical course (proteinuria, anemia) but no new genetic or functional evidence about the variant.
